extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set is partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, where the Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm. The dataset contains only natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human tests), and is the largest public-domain set of this kind (7,787 questions).
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions drawn from a variety of sources, specifically standardized tests for grades 3-9. The collection process involved several months of extensive search and investigation to obtain these questions, as most examination boards release only limited practice tests. Additionally, the ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run search queries relevant to science topics, collecting and de-duplicating documents, stripping content to text, and chunking into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Standardized science tests from various sources (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, etc.) and web-scraped science-related sentences.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions) and an Easy Set (5197 questions). Challenge questions were defined as those answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm (IR solver) and a word co-occurrence algorithm (PMI solver).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, documents were collected via search queries, de-duplicated, stripped to text, and chunked into sentences. For the ARC Dataset, questions were sorted into Challenge and Easy sets based on baseline performance. For baseline experiments, questions and answer options were converted into hypothesis sentences for entailment models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The questions were authored by humans for standardized tests. The ARC Corpus was created automatically via web scraping and search queries. No manual human annotation of labels for the ARC dataset items is described beyond the original test authors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The challenge aims to address limitations in previous datasets that focused on retrieval-style tasks, encouraging progress on questions requiring reasoning, use of commonsense knowledge, or other advanced methods for deeper text comprehension.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards US elementary and middle school science topics. The Challenge Set definition relies on the failure of specific simple algorithms (IR and PMI), which may introduce biases related to the types of reasoning those algorithms fail to capture.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The questions are drawn from US elementary and middle school standardized tests, limiting generalizability to other educational systems or age groups. The Challenge Set definition is an approximation of 'hard' questions based on simple baseline failures. The ARC Corpus, while extensive, may not contain all necessary knowledge explicitly, requiring complex reasoning to exploit distributed evidence.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is posed as a challenge to the community to develop more advanced QA methods that go beyond simple retrieval or word correlation.
